front: Why custom sign-in branding is a security control
back: A user who knows what their own sign-in page looks like has a chance of spotting a fake one. Keyword: familiarity defeats phishing.

front: Verified domain vs domain in use
back: Verification proves ownership; assigning services decides what it carries. A verified domain not assigned to Exchange accepts no mail. Keyword: two separate steps.

front: Why a domain will not delete
back: Some object still references it. Domain removal is an object hunt, not a delete. Keyword: find the references first.
Service health notifications are not configured by default. Set which administrators receive which alerts. Keyword: nobody is paged by default.
Membership drives entitlement, so joiners gain and leavers lose licences automatically. Direct assignment is what leaves you paying for leavers. Keyword: entitlement follows membership.

front: Not enough licence units in a group
back: Members land in an error state rather than being silently skipped, reported per user on the group's licence page. Keyword: errors, not silence.
Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Agent 365, and Copilot Studio each license separately on top of the base plan. Keyword: three more line items.
Retention decides how long content is kept and stops permanent removal. Backup restores content to a previous state after corruption. Keyword: keep, or roll back.
Traffic hairpinned through a distant central egress or proxy. Microsoft 365 traffic should reach the service as directly as possible. Keyword: break out locally.

front: Retaining a leaver's mail without a licence
back: Convert the user mailbox to a shared mailbox. Shared needs no licence until it exceeds the size limit or needs its own archive. Keyword: convert to shared.

front: Copilot in a Teams meeting needs what?
back: Transcription or recording — it is a prerequisite, not an option. The during-only vs during-and-after setting is a governance choice. Keyword: no transcript, no Copilot.
The user is synchronised from on-premises Active Directory, so the source of authority is on-premises. Edit it there. Keyword: source of authority wins.

External collaboration decides who may invite guests and what guests see. Cross-tenant access decides which partner tenants are trusted, including accepting their MFA. Keyword: who invites, or who is trusted.

front: A dynamic group that stays empty
back: Its rule reads an attribute nobody populates. Dynamic membership is only as good as the attribute behind it. Keyword: populate the attribute.
Security groups grant access. Microsoft 365 groups additionally provision a mailbox, a SharePoint site, and a team. Keyword: access, or workspace.
That phrasing is asking for Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Keyword: bulk means Graph PowerShell.

A standing role assignment becomes eligible — activated for a bounded period with approval, justification, and MFA. A compromised account is no longer automatically a compromised admin. Keyword: eligible, not permanent.

front: Manage some users but not all
back: An administrative unit scopes a role to a subset of the directory. The role says what; the unit says to whom. Keyword: scope the role.
SMS and voice — phishable and interceptable. Passkeys and Windows Hello for Business are phishing-resistant because the credential binds to device and site. Keyword: move off telephony.
Password Protection needs agents on the domain controllers to extend the ban to on-premises AD, or the weak password syncs up. Keyword: deploy the DC agents.

front: Three ways "it won't let me in"
back: First factor, second factor, or a Conditional Access grant control. The sign-in logs say which. Keyword: find the stage first.

front: Do Conditional Access policies override each other?
back: No. They are additive and all matching policies must be satisfied — block always wins over allow. Keyword: everything must pass.

front: The policy that locks out the tenant
back: Require compliant device, all users, no exclusions. Always exclude emergency access accounts and test in report-only mode first. Keyword: break-glass and report-only.
User risk = the identity is likely compromised, so force a password change. Sign-in risk = this sign-in is likely not them, so require MFA. Keyword: who, or which attempt.

front: Why Safe Links checks at click time
back: A link benign at delivery can be weaponised afterwards. Rewriting and checking on click catches that. Keyword: delivery-time checks are not enough.

front: A Defender policy that never applies
back: A broader custom policy sits above it in priority order, and the first matching policy of each type wins. Keyword: check the priority order.

front: The number to watch on attack simulation
back: Not the click rate, but whether it moves after training. A stable rate means the training is not working. Keyword: measure the change.
It shows what would have matched without blocking anyone. A policy generating alerts everyone ignores is worse than none. Keyword: measure before enforcing.
It can stop labelled content being used in Copilot responses — so a document the user can open is still excluded from what Copilot will cite. Keyword: readable but not citable.
Retention wins over deletion, and the longest retention wins. That is why overlapping policies keep far more than intended. Keyword: longest retention wins.
Not "is Copilot secure" but "what is our Copilot reaching" — which sensitive data AI touches and where oversharing exposes it. Keyword: start data readiness here.
Never. It answers from what the asking user can already open, so it makes existing access visible rather than creating it. Keyword: it reveals, it does not grant.
The oversharing predates it and remains — merely harder to notice again. The remediation is permissions work. Keyword: hiding is not fixing.

front: Search made it reachable; Copilot made it what?
back: Conversationally reachable. The difference is practice, not permission — which is why the fix is upstream. Keyword: same access, new habit.
Measure with oversharing reports and DSPM, remediate with owners through access reviews, protect with labels and DLP, exclude last. Keyword: exclusions come last.
Excludes a site from Copilot and organisation-wide search without changing who can open it directly. The surgical option. Keyword: hidden from Copilot, still available.

front: Who should run a site access review?
back: The site owner, not the tenant administrator — they are the only ones who know who should have access. Keyword: push it to the owner.

front: The cost of allowing Copilot web search
back: Better answers, and query context leaving the organisation's boundary. A deliberate tenant-level decision, not a default. Keyword: grounding vs boundary.
Results from a connected external source are trimmed to what the asking user may see in that source system. Keyword: the index respects the source.
Lets users buy their own AI licences without procurement. Off in most governed tenants for exactly that reason. Keyword: turn it off deliberately.

front: What Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives an agent
back: A first-class directory identity, so it can be granted, reviewed, audited, and revoked like any principal — and its actions are attributable. Keyword: agents become principals.

front: Governing an agent uses which machinery?
back: The ordinary one — access packages with approval and expiry, Conditional Access, and lifecycle workflows. Keyword: no parallel regime.

front: The control most often skipped on agents
back: A named owner. An unowned agent is never reviewed, never updated, never decommissioned. Keyword: require an owner at creation.

front: What the agent registry is for
back: Discovery of what exists, a publish-or-reject review workflow, and per-agent control over install, block, and access — including custom uploads. Keyword: inventory plus gate.

front: Why set agent settings before reviewing agents
back: Allowed types, sharing, templates, and who may install decide the shape of the queue. An open tenant produces a queue nobody reads. Keyword: constrain first, review second.
Not only "is this agent useful" but "does it hold only the tools its job requires". An unused tool is standing exposure. Keyword: least privilege for agents.
Approval at publish time says nothing about behaviour six months later. Agent 365 monitoring is the continuing half. Keyword: watch after you approve.
Per-user licences, paid whether used or not; and consumption, which moves with what agents do. Forecast both separately. Keyword: fixed plus variable.
An adoption problem no further licensing fixes. Watch active use, not licences assigned. Keyword: measure use, not entitlement.
Could be a genuine service incident, a data problem, or a prompt problem. Only service health for AI services distinguishes them. Keyword: check health before blaming the model.
